goal.problem: core/startup.py still reads the old monolithic notes.jsonl for startup injection, and skill templates (backfill-handoffs, wrapup) still write notes using patterns that assume the old JSONL layout.
goal.solution: Update startup injection to read per-folder indexes and only the latest handoff .md file. Update skill templates and scribe/CLAUDE.md to document the new storage model.
goal.value: Completes the end-to-end switchover: sessions start with lean index-based context injection, and all automated note-writing paths produce v2-format output.

components.name: startup.py rewrite
components.description: core/startup.py run_summary() reads each type's index.jsonl instead of notes.jsonl. Active items list uses summary field from indexes. Latest handoff section reads one .md file instead of dumping full JSONL content.

components.name: backfill-handoffs template update
components.description: core/commands/backfill-handoffs.md agent prompt updated to write handoffs using the new CLI patterns (notes.py add --type handoff still works, just documenting new storage expectations).

components.name: wrapup skill update
components.description: Update the wrapup skill template to reference the new storage model when writing end-of-session handoffs.

components.name: scribe/CLAUDE.md update
components.description: Document the new folder-per-type storage model, updated CLI examples, and the general type.

shape.pattern: Startup injection already reads JSONL and formats summaries — same output format, different data source.
shape.data_flow: Session start -> core/startup.py -> glob type folders -> read each index.jsonl -> format summaries + read latest handoff .md -> inject into prompt.
shape.dependencies: Phases 1-3 complete (store.py exists, notes.py rewired, data migrated).

behavior.input: Session start triggers startup hook which calls run_summary().
behavior.processing: 1. run_summary() imports ScribeStore or reads indexes directly. 2. For active items: read each type's index.jsonl, collect entries with status='active', format as 'ID type (age) summary'. 3. For latest handoff: find most recent entry in handoffs/index.jsonl, read its .md file for full content. 4. Inject into startup context — same format as before but sourced from indexes.
behavior.output: Startup context block with active items list and latest handoff summary. Output format identical to current behavior.

error_cases.trigger: No type folders exist yet (fresh install, pre-migration)
error_cases.behavior: Fall back to reading old JSONL if it exists, or return empty context.

error_cases.trigger: Index file missing for a type

edge_cases.condition: Both old JSONL and new layout exist (mid-migration)
edge_cases.behavior: Prefer new layout if any type folder has an index.jsonl.
Skip the latest handoff section. Same as current behavior.

in_scope: Rewrite run_summary() to read from folder-per-type indexes
Read latest handoff .md file only (not full JSONL dump)
Update wrapup skill template if needed
Backwards-compatible fallback to old JSONL during transition
out_of_scope: Changes to store.py or notes.py — Phases 1-2
must_not_break: Startup injection output format (other hooks may parse it)
Budgeter hooks that extract session IDs from startup context

acceptance_criteria: Given the v2 layout with notes across multiple types, when a session starts, then the startup context contains all active notes formatted as 'ID type (age) summary'
Given a recent handoff exists in handoffs/, when startup runs, then only the summary and a pointer to the full .md file are injected (not the full body)
Given no type folders exist but old notes.jsonl does, when startup runs, then it falls back to the old JSONL reading
Given the backfill agent runs, when it writes a handoff note, then the note appears correctly in handoffs/ folder
Given scribe/CLAUDE.md is read by a new session, then it documents the folder-per-type model, the general type, and updated CLI examples
